title: Envoys meet Putin, missiles hit Kyiv, and Iran strikes an Omani island
summary: US envoys meet Putin in Moscow a day after the Abu Dhabi talks, Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles hours after those talks end, Ukrainian drones reach the Omsk refinery deep in Siberia, Iran attacks navigation systems on Oman's Didamar Island and another tanker is struck in Hormuz, and an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Gaza kills six.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Thursday, November twelfth. Yesterday the Abu Dhabi talks ended with a prisoner exchange deal. Today, the diplomacy moved to Moscow.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The American envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, met President Putin at the Kremlin. Witkoff pointed to that prisoner exchange as a sign that, in his words, progress is being made in resolving the conflict.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And Kushner raised Europe. He told Putin that Europeans are showing a desire to take part in negotiations.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Putin's answer was pointed. He said Europe should work out whether it wants peace or war.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So that question, who sits at the table, is still open. After Moscow, the envoys are due to fly to Dublin to brief President Zelensky.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And remember the read from the Institute for the Study of War this week. It assesses that the Kremlin is trying to steer these talks toward a bigger bargain over European security, reviving the demands it made of NATO in twenty twenty-one.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Which would explain why Moscow wants to decide when, and how, Europe comes in.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Meanwhile, the war carried on. Hours after the talks in Abu Dhabi ended, Russia attacked Kyiv and the surrounding area with ballistic missiles and drones.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Kyiv's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, reported one person killed and eight injured. Ukraine's Air Force says Russia launched a hundred and twenty-three attack drones, and eighty-nine were shot down.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And Ukraine's long-range campaign reached further than ever. Its Special Operations Forces confirmed a drone strike on the Omsk refinery, in Siberia. That's about two thousand five hundred kilometres from Ukraine.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Omsk is described as Russia's largest refinery. Air raid sirens sounded in the city for more than eight hours, and the regional governor reported falling drone debris. How much damage was done isn't confirmed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Put that next to the last few days. Kirishi on Monday. The port of Ust-Luga on Wednesday. Now Omsk. Ukraine is clearly going after Russia's oil system, from the Baltic coast to Siberia.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the ground, a small but notable change. The Institute for the Study of War assessed that Russian forces advanced in the centre of Bilytske, a town southeast of Dobropillia. That's based on footage published on Tuesday.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: But east of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, it says Russian attacks on Tuesday and Wednesday gained no ground.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Now to the Gulf, and something new. Reuters, citing three sources, reports that Iran attacked ship navigation systems on Didamar Island. That's a small Omani island right in the Strait of Hormuz.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Iranian state media said the Revolutionary Guard destroyed what it called enemy navigation systems. Reuters confirmed smoke over the island, but couldn't verify what was actually hit.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Shipping sources told Reuters they expect only a limited effect on traffic, because other navigation systems exist elsewhere. But it is a strike on Omani territory, not just on ships passing by.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And the attacks on ships continue. Today the British maritime agency UKMTO said a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile while passing through the strait. It classed it as an attack. All the crew are safe.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Separately, Iran's army and Revolutionary Guard said two supertankers, carrying more than four million barrels between them, caught fire after hitting mines east of the strait. Independent monitors haven't confirmed that.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: It's not clear whether those are the same ships. That's now three straight days of reported hits on tankers, after the one off Limah on Tuesday and the ADNOC vessel in Emirati waters.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the diplomacy, Iran is holding its line. It again denied that it's negotiating with Washington, and said the strait will stay shut until its demands are met.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Qatar, the mediator, says there is progress, but that it can't say how near or far a deal is. And CBS reports President Trump saying the war will be put away very soon, quote, one way or the other.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Gaza, the deadliest single incident on today's map. Gaza's Health Ministry says an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis hit the surgical wing and killed at least six people, including a doctor and a child.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The ministry says at least twenty-eight people were wounded. Other health officials put it at twenty. Israel said it was targeting a Hamas commander and other militants.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That comes a day after local health officials said Israeli airstrikes killed three people in Gaza City, including two brothers. The strikes are continuing despite the ceasefire that's formally in place.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: One housekeeping note. The strike archive behind the site's new Strike data charts grew by five entries today, and now holds a hundred and eighteen strikes going back to early October.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: A couple of updates to stories from earlier this week. On Wednesday's Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition now says it intercepted three cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh, two drones headed for Mecca and the south, and two ballistic missiles headed west.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: The Houthis say they hit an airport and oil sites, and they deny targeting Mecca. None of that is independently verified.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And in Sudan, the drone strike in Blue Nile state on Tuesday. A local governor has named the village as Bani Shako, and says drones from the Rapid Support Forces killed nine residents. The group hasn't commented.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the ships, nothing confirmed today. The Theodore Roosevelt left Singapore earlier this week heading for the Middle East, and estimates of when it reaches the Arabian Sea range from about now to late next week. So its marker on the map is still an estimate.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: The George Washington and the George H. W. Bush remain in the Arabian Sea. The next USNI fleet tracker, due Monday, should settle where the Roosevelt is.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: So, what to watch. What the envoys tell Zelensky in Dublin, and the details of the prisoner exchange. How Oman responds to the strike on Didamar Island. And whether Trump's 'one way or the other' means a deal with Iran, or something else.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
